entities.summary: Sir Alured Clarke was a British Army officer. He took charge of all British troops in Georgia in May 1780 and was then deployed to Philadelphia to supervise the evacuation of British prisoners of war at the closing stages of the American Revolutionary War. He went on to be Governor of Jamaica and then lieutenant-governor of Lower Canada in which role he had responsibility for implementing the Constitutional Act 1791. He was then sent to India where he became Commander-in-Chief of the Madras Army, then briefly Governor-General of India and finally Commander-in-Chief of India during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Governor of Jamaica and Lieutenant-Governor of Lower Canada, Clarke played a crucial role in implementing the Constitutional Act 1791, which significantly impacted the governance of British North America. His subsequent appointment as Commander-in-Chief of India during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War demonstrates his broader regional influence.
